flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c3 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: Eval dropped 39cp and you still called it strongest. c3 does not claim the center; it prepares d4. That is the MacLeod idea. Paste-the-center-control on a waiting pawn is how every opening ply starts to sound the same.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your e-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: d4 is defended by c3 and the queen. This is the normal exchange after White's d4 break, not a hanging pawn. doubled_pawns in the reasons is fiction: nobody gets doubled pawns by this capture. Stop tagging defended center pawns as hanging.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: The pawn on d4 is defended by the knight on c6. I recaptured. I did not win material. wins_material plus 'undefended' on an equal recapture is a lie, and now I will side-eye every later hanging warning.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to b4 is the strongest move because it puts the opponent in check.
flags.critique: I can see the plus sign. Teach the idea: develop with check, hassle the king, pin or force a piece to c3. 'Strongest because check' is a caption, not a lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Blank on the move that hits the knight on c6. That is the whole point of pushing d4-d5: tempo on the piece, space, the knight has to run. I got a verdict with no because and empty reasons. If kicked_by_pawn exists in the stack, use it.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your c6-knight to e5 leaves you with a backward pawn. A better move would have been taking the knight on c3 with your b4-bishop because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: 296cp and you lectured me about a backward pawn. The knight was attacked by d5, so it had to move — but e5 walks into Qa4+, a fork of my king and the bishop on b4. That is the tactic this whole stretch is about. Bxc3+ is check and wrecks the queenside; 'pin the pawn to the rook' never names b2/Ra1 and is not why I should have taken.

flags.quote: Moving your g1-knight to f3 is a blunder, but moving your queen to a4 would be better because you fork the black king and the black b4-bishop and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: The fork is the first honest sentence in the game. Then you glued on 'and then pin the pawn to the rook' from some later PV ghost. Qa4+ wins the bishop; it does not pin a pawn to a rook. Reasons on the played move are development and center_control, which describe Nf3, not why it is a 337cp blunder.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to g4 is a blunder, but moving your c8-bishop to d7 would be better because you can likely take a knight.
flags.critique: Bd7 does not take a knight. It sits on the a4-e8 diagonal so Qa4+ is no longer check, which is how you stop the fork. 'You can likely take a knight' is a PV capture sold as the reason for a quiet prophylactic move. I still have not been told my bishop on b4 is hanging to that queen check.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to e2 is a blunder, but moving your queen to a4 would be better because you fork the black king and the black b4-bishop and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: Same missed fork, same leftover pin clause, second time in three plies. I am in a tactics puzzle and you keep developing. If Qa4+ was the answer last move, it is still the answer. Drop the pin sludge and stop praising development on a piece-winning check.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on f3 with your e5-knight puts it where the white e2-bishop and pawn can take and you lose a knight.
flags.critique: I took a knight. They recapture. That is a trade, not 'you lose a knight.' The hanging template scored the recapture as a piece loss and ignored that I just captured the same piece. Lichess called this an inaccuracy; you said mistake. Either way the chess in the sentence is wrong.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on f3 with your e2-bishop is a mistake because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: If the knight were undefended, taking it would not be a mistake. It is defended by the bishop on g4. That is why Bxf3 is worse than gxf3: the pawn recapture hits g4. You used the successful-capture because-clause on a classified mistake. Backwards. Also 'you can likely take a bishop' on gxf3 is the hedge talking; just say the f-pawn attacks the bishop.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on f3 with your g4-bishop puts it where the white queen and pawn can take and you lose a knight.
flags.critique: I traded bishops. There is no knight on that square. materialLabel is calling a bishop-sized SEE 'a knight' because 300cp clears the knight threshold. I recaptured a bishop and you told me I hung a knight. I cannot learn piece values from this.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on f3 with your queen is a mistake because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: Same inversion as Bxf3: recapturing an 'undefended' piece is the reason you give for a mistake. The real miss is still Qa4+, the fork you named two moves ago and then let me recapture past. If the queen take is wrong, say I missed the check that wins the bishop on b4.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to c5 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the king.
flags.critique: Queen on b3 was eating the bishop on b4. Bc5 saves the piece. You tagged hanging and saves_piece and then taught a nameless pin of f2. Lead with: the bishop was hanging to the queen, you tucked it onto the diagonal. Then mention the pin and name f2.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to g4 leaves your pawn hanging to the white queen. A better move would have been moving your f8-rook to e8 because your rook gets a semi-open file.
flags.critique: b7 has been staring at Qb3 since ply 25. Ng4 did not hang it. You are firing ignored_threat at a pawn that was already hanging, then suggesting Re8 for a semi-open file like every other 'there's better.' If the knight move is the inaccuracy, tell me what it walked off or into.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: h3 hits the knight on g4. Empty reasons. This is the kick I can see with my eyes. If you cannot say 'you chase the knight,' I do not know what the detector is for.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: White just played h3 attacking my knight. I leave it and counterattack the bishop on g3. That is a piece trade / desperado, and you gave me strongest-move plus duplicate ignored_threat in the dump. Name the trade: knight hangs, you take the bishop anyway.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on g3 with your h-pawn is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: White just took my knight on g4. I take a bishop. That is knight for bishop, not 'a bishop ahead.' SEE on this ply does not know about last ply. 'Defender of the white pawn' never says which pawn. I traded pieces in a melee and you told me I won a piece.

flags.quote: Moving your c1-rook to c3 is playable, but taking the bishop on c5 with your c1-rook would be better because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: Rxc5 takes a bishop. You sold it as king safety. Maybe removing the bishop that points at f2 makes the king happier, but that is not why a 1200 should take the piece. Say you win the bishop, or rook-for-bishop plus the follow-up on c5. King-safer is the wrong headline.

flags.quote: Moving your a8-rook to c8 is the strongest move because your rook can use an open file.
flags.critique: The queen is sitting on c5. I put a rook on the same file as the queen. That is attacking the queen, not 'using an open file.' File jargon without the target is how you make positional words feel like filler.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 gives the opponent more access to your king. A better move would have been moving your queen to e3.
flags.critique: 206cp, Lichess blunder, and Qe3 has no because. King-more-exposed is plausible — I poked a hole and Rc2 lands on the seventh next — but a SAN with no idea is not a lesson. Why e3: trade queens, cover the second rank, get off a7. Pick one.

flags.quote: Moving your e8-rook to c8 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: I doubled rooks on the c-file, with one already on the seventh. Empty sentence. Doubling is a club-player word I would actually reuse. You had rook_on_seventh last move and then went mute.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to d1 is a blunder, but taking the rook on c1 with your rook would be better because you take the defender of the black c8-rook.
flags.critique: Rc1 pins my rook to the king and my knight is hanging to the queen on b2. Rxc1 takes the pinning rook. The c1 rook is not 'the defender of the c8-rook' in any tactic I can use. removed_defender hallucinated a stack. Teach: you are pinned, take the rook, do not drop a knight on the pin line.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on b2 with your knight is the strongest move because you come out a rook ahead and it unveils an attack from your rook on the black c1-rook.
flags.critique: I took a queen. The discovered rook hit on c1 is real and useful. 'A rook ahead' is SEE after their rook recaptures the knight, then materialLabel maps 600cp to a rook. I captured a queen; say queen, or queen for knight. Do not make me do arithmetic to decode the piece I just took.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but taking the knight on b2 with your rook lets white force checkmate in 6 moves. This lets white force checkmate in 6 moves. A better move would have been moving your pawn to b6.
flags.critique: You said the mate sentence twice. containsIgnoreCase is not catching 'this lets white force checkmate' against the problem clause. Lichess called it a mistake; you said blunder, which is fair given mate-in-6. Then b6 with no because. If I am getting mated, tell me why b6 stops it, and say the mate once.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures hanging or winning
suggestions.detail: exd4, cxd4, Nxf3+, Qxf3, Kxf1 all fired hanging or wins_material on equal recaptures. Gate those kinds on SEE net versus the position before the capture sequence, or suppress when the captured unit arrived last ply. A 1200 recapturing on d4 will not believe you when a rook actually hangs.

suggestions.title: Do not justify mistakes with capture-success copy
suggestions.detail: Bxf3 and Qxf3 used concept capture, so explainPlayedAsBenefit kept 'the piece was undefended' as the because on a classified mistake. If classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, take playedBecause from problemReasons, not pickBenefitReasons. The 1200 hears: taking a free piece is wrong, which trains the opposite of tactics.

suggestions.title: Prefer a pending queen fork over backward-pawn copy
suggestions.detail: Ne5 lost 296cp to Qa4+ forking king and Bb4, and copy taught a backward pawn. When the refutation PV starts with a check that attacks two pieces, lead with fork even if backward_pawn ranks first. Same stretch: Bg4/Be2/Qxf3 kept missing or sludge-coating that fork. Club players will remember one named double attack.

suggestions.title: Do not sell PV captures as reasons for quiet moves
suggestions.detail: Bd7 was 'you can likely take a knight'; Qa4+ was fork 'and then pin the pawn to the rook.' verifyLikelyTactics is attaching later line events to the first move. Only use likely capture/pin/fork when the suggested move itself makes that tactic, or name the follow-up as a second sentence after the prophylactic idea (Bd7 blocks Qa4+).

suggestions.title: Say when a pawn hits a piece
suggestions.detail: d5 vs Nc6 and h3 vs Ng4 were strongest-move with empty reasons. kicked_by_pawn already exists; pickBenefitReasons is not leading with it on the attacker's move. If a pawn move attacks an enemy piece, the because should name that piece. Center-control and silence are why the opening and the h3 kick taught nothing.

suggestions.title: Never emit a better-move SAN with no idea
suggestions.detail: Qf3, e5, b4, Qe3, b6 all appeared as bare alternatives. skipSuggestionLecture should not apply once evalLoss is in inaccuracy range, and suggestedBecause should come from suggestedBenefits even if the list is short. A 1200 staring at Qe3 after a 200cp hole needs 'cover the second rank' or 'offer the queen trade,' not a coordinate.

suggestions.title: Name the target on a file, not just the file
suggestions.detail: Rac8 'uses an open file' while the queen sits on c5; Rec8 doubling was blank; Rxc5 was sold as king safety. If a rook move attacks a piece on that file, lead with the attack. If two rooks share a file, say doubled. Rank attack / doubling / rook_on_seventh above open_file and king_safer when both fire.

suggestions.title: Fix bishop-as-knight labels and duplicate mate lines
suggestions.detail: Bxf3 said 'lose a knight' because materialLabel maps 250–399 to knight, so a bishop SEE becomes a knight. Nxb2 taking a queen became 'a rook ahead' from net SEE after recapture. Prefer the captured piece name on a winning capture; keep net labels for true exchanges. Mate: allows_mate problem plus consequence both render 'lets white force checkmate in N'; containsIgnoreCase(slice 24) misses the 'this' prefix — dedupe on mateIn.

whatWorked: Qa4+ copy actually named the fork of king and Bb4 — the one true tactic in the opening mess.
Castling on plies 21 and 28 names shelter plus rook activation without fluff.
Qb3 and Qd2 correctly say the queen is fleeing a knight (Ne5, then Nh3).
Qg5 naming the pin of the g-pawn to the queen is specific enough to reuse.
Rc2 'rook on the seventh' and d6 'passed pawn' are real endgame words.
Rc1 pin of rook to king plus discovered queen hit on the knight is the best sentence in the dump.
R8c2 correctly flags the queen hanging to Nd1; Qd4+ correctly names the fork that starts the mate.
